title: Parquet-tiered ingest + Loki/Elasticsearch compatibility bridge for tenant-aware structured logs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a compatibility bridge that accepts high-throughput structured JSON logs and writes them to a hot Loki-compatible stream for low-latency querying while simultaneously producing columnar Parquet batches and Elastic-compatible bulk payloads for medium/long-term analytics. The bridge should be tenant-aware (per-tenant label and field filtering), preserve and canonicalize correlation IDs, and support schema evolution without full re-ingest.

Scope:
- Input: JSONL / structured log HTTP/gRPC intake from sidecars and runtime SDKs.
- Hot-path: normalize fields, apply per-tenant label mapping, emit a compact Loki log line with labels (tenant_id, env, service, corr_id) and a base64 compressed payload when size warrants.
- Cold-path: buffer/compact into Parquet row-groups partitioned by tenant/date/service, and generate Elastic bulk API documents with mapped field types for full-text and numeric queries.
- Schema management: integrate with the schema registry to support optional/unknown fields and provide backward/forward compatibility routines (flattening, renaming policies).
- Operational: backpressure semantics, dynamic tenant sampling, auditable routing decisions, and cost-based retention hooks.

Non-goals: deep log enrichment (separate enrichers will own geo/rdns), or replacing existing long-term cold-storage pipelines. We are building a compatibility layer only.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end prototype handling 10k EPS of 1KB JSON events with <50ms p50 hot-path latency in canary tenant.
- Deterministic corr_id canonicalization across multi-hop (sidecar -> gateway -> bridge).
- Successful roundtrip of unknown field evolution (add/remove) without dropping events for 30 days of synthetic traffic.
- Demonstrable queries in Loki and Elasticsearch for the same event IDs within 2 minutes of ingest.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Label explosion in Loki: implement tenant label prefixing and configurable cardinality caps with automatic field demotion to payload.
- Schema drift causing indexing errors in ES: implement schema validation and a type-coercion policy with reject/route-to-parquet fallback.
- Backpressure cascades: build token-bucket admission + prioritized hot-pathing for critical tenant SLAs.

Rollout plan: prototype -> internal perf run (dev cluster) -> canary with 2-3 low-traffic tenants -> opt-in beta -> full rollout with migration docs and a toggle in Console.
comments: 2026-03-03 - Architecture review scheduled with infra, runtime, and security (meeting notes in Confluence).

2026-03-05 - Prototype spike: implemented Kafka producer + Loki push adapter; measured hot-path p50 ~42ms for 5k EPS in dev harness (link to benchmark graph: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingest/proto-hotpath).

2026-03-07 - Design review: decided to use a two-tier buffering strategy (memory LRU + spill to s3) for Parquet row-group assembly. Review feedback: add configurable tenant quotas and a safety valve to drop non-critical fields under memory pressure.

2026-03-09 - Security feedback: require encryption-at-rest for Parquet blobs and KMS integration for keys; noted requirement to add an audit log entry for field demotions. Assigned to SEC-REVIEW backlog.

2026-03-10 - Prototype PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-bridge/pull/142 (includes Loki adapter, Parquet writer, and schema-registry client). CI failing on integration test due to ES mapping rejection — investigation blocking canary timeline.
